en.title: Splits Where the Number of Shared Distinct Letters Strictly Exceeds a Threshold
en.description:
Split the whole string into two non-empty contiguous parts; the number of distinct letters that appear in both parts must be strictly greater than k. Find the number of valid split positions; this does not count repeated occurrences of shared characters.

This site independently wrote the standard I/O, editorial and tests; missing original bounds and corrections to examples are stated explicitly in the statement.
en.input: The string and k are given, separated by whitespace. Original bounds: a lowercase string of length 1..100000, and 0≤k≤26.
en.output: Output a single integer, the answer.
en.explanation: The outputs of the three public examples are 2; 0; and 0, checked by independent enumeration or direct simulation.
hints: Maintain the 26 left and 26 right frequencies and the number of letters present on both sides. Each time a character moves from the right part to the left part, first subtract its old contribution to the intersection, then add its new contribution; only check the first n−1 cuts.
